<!-- pr-reviewer: 7ab1d7689123cfc754d9592ac27bc62f2a11181f -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after #964, #975 and #1025, in that order).

This was a high-tier review because the change affects posted G-code. I read the seat logic looking for ways to break it and ran extra probe streams through the post.

### Scope
- `origin/main..7ab1d768` is #1025's head (`1f156d30`) plus this PR's one commit. The parent of `7ab1d768` is exactly `1f156d30`, and nothing else rides along.
- This PR's own diff (`1f156d30..7ab1d768`) touches `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `crates/app/tests/lathe_cycle_exit.rs`, `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_refusals.rs` and `docs/decisions/1026-lathe-cycle-seat.md`. It changes no golden. The one-line change to `fanuc-lathe/axial_drill.nc` (`G00 X0 Z30` exit) is #1025's.
- It adds no snapshot PNGs, process files, dependencies, build.rs or scripts.

### What looks good
- `cycleSeat` (fanuc-lathe.cps, the `#1026` block above `onCycle`) replaces the single diagonal `G00 X0 Z<R>` with these steps: Z out to R when below it, then X onto centre, then Z down to R when above it.
  - `G80` is written only when a group is open. `chainRapid` and `endPreamble` already clear `inCycle`, so G80 is never doubled.
  - When the tool is already seated, the output is byte-for-byte what it was before (same as the old `!inCycle` / `there` guard).
- The post seats only from a position it can trust:
  - `seatKnown` is reset in `onSection` and set by every motion hook.
  - The engine's `currentPosition` is the previous stream move's end (`engine.rs` `set_current(pos)` before each hook).
  - A cycle that is its section's first motion is therefore refused rather than positioned from an assumed tool-change spot.
  - I checked that the generator never emits that case: `drilling/cycle.rs` stamps `first_move` only after the approach, and `posting.rs` places the Cycle record at that move. So the new refusal blocks nothing the shipped generators produce, and the two synthetic fixtures in `lathe_post_refusals.rs` were changed honestly to match real streams.
- Refusals go through `refuse()` into `out.warnings`, which `posting.rs:465` turns into a refused post. Nothing posts silently.
- Units: the below/above test compares `currentPosition.Z` with `R` in the same stream frame. X is judged against `orgX`/`orgY` and written as `xWord(0)`, so diameter vs radius and inch output do not enter the comparison.
- The read-back checker and the revert check described in the body hold.

### Local results (trial-merged with origin/main 23c62044, merged cleanly; debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build (`cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run`, 19 binaries) | ok |
| lathe_cycle_exit | 6 passed |
| lathe_post_refusals | 7 passed |
| c_axis_live | 5 passed |
| c_axis_unwind | 7 passed |
| lathe_post | 7 passed |
| lathe_post_g76 | 8 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| golden_cl | 25 passed |
| drilling_axial | 7 passed |
| inverted_post | 15 passed |
| comment_escape / control_comp / coolant_followups / wear_comp | 3 / 5 / 7 / 5 passed |
| lathe_blade_corner / lathe_nose_tip / lathe_spindle_law | 4 / 6 / 8 passed |
| program_entry / turning_face_approach | 9 / 3 passed |
| camcraft-post `comp` | 9 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I also ran a local probe test (not kept) through the merged post:
- **On axis, below R** (Z15, R22): `G00 Z22`, then `G83`. Correct.
- **At R, off centre** (radius 15): `G00 X0`, then `G83`. Correct.
- **Exit to clearance, then a second cycle** (G83, then G85): `G80` once per group, then `G00 Z22`, then `G85`. No doubled G80.
- **Open group whose chain ended at the bottom, then another cycle:** `G80`, `G00 Z22`, `G83`. The machine is already back at R after the canned cycle, so this Z move is redundant but harmless.
- **R equal to the bottom, off seat:** refused by name, no cycle written.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. The "bottom below R" check runs only when a seat move is needed. A cycle read already on its seat with `bottom >= R` still posts as before (e.g. `G83 Z30` from R22). No shipped generator emits that, and this is not a regression, but the body's "the post checks it" is true only on the hop path. A one-line follow-up could move the check ahead of the `already on its seat` return.
2. Two cycles in one open group with no exit between them post as `G83 ...` then `G84 ...` with no `G80` and no re-seat. Fanuc accepts this as a modal switch, and the old code did the same. Noted only because the brief asked about it.
3. The hop law's "Z out first" assumes a pure +Z at the current X is clear: true for the face/OD approaches the drill streams use. Behind a shoulder or in an undercut it would not be, but neither was the old diagonal, and the stream reached that spot on its own moves.
4. Not exercised: a real control or simulator run; G84/G85 seated from off the seat (same code path as G83); an inverted-Z machine (`invert::apply` mirrors the stream before the post).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
